newsitem.title: USA: EU ministers to brief G7 on Amsterdam, euro.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to brief G7 on Amsterdam, euro.

text.p: European finance ministers and officials were due to brief their partners in the Group of Seven on Friday on the latest steps towards launching a single currency in 1999 and its implications for countries outside Europe.

A European Union diplomat said they would discuss agreements reached at an EU summit in Amsterdam on Monday on a stability pact limiting budget deficits under monetary union and on action to boost growth and jobs, he said.
European ministers were expected to reassure their partners that the plans for a single currency were "firmly on track", the diplomat said.

G7 finance ministers, meeting separately on Friday night on the fringes of a summit of heads of state and government, could look briefly at the implications of the euro's launch on the dollar and the yen.
European ministers have generally said they do not expect any major upheaval from the launch of the euro, with any effect on international asset allocation showing only gradually.
The question of who would represent the euro-zone at international meetings could also be raised, although little real discussion was expected on this, the diplomat said.
Europe has only just begun itself to look at the question, agreeing in Amsterdam to start studies into how the euro zone should be represented at international meetings.
The Group of Seven comprises four of the 15 European Union countries -- Britain, France, Germany and Italy -- alongside the United States, Canada and Japan.

A spokeswoman for French President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday that G7 leaders would discuss the euro at their economic talks on Saturday and were expected to make a "clearly positive" statement about Europe's plans for single currency.
